<description>
IsRoutable() doesn't exclude multicast (224.0.0.0/4, ff00::/8), so multicast addresses received over gossip can end up in addrman.

This adds IsMulticast() and excludes it in IsRoutable().

Test updates:
- addrman_getaddr: expected counts change, since its generated addresses include the multicast range.
- The last asmap test vector was a multicast address. I replaced it with a non-multicast one at the top of the range (same AS).
</description>

I think it's OK to do this, but it does not actually solve a problem. Here's a more complete branch I worked on a few months ago covering more addresses ranges: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/compare/master...0xB10C:bitcoin:2026-09-reserved-networks

I did not PR this for two reasons:

1. The needed diff is quite large as the `250.x.x.x` addresses used in `src/test/addrman_tests.cpp` would all need to change
2. It actually does not matter in practice. If someone wants to send unreachable addresses, they still can. They are going to pick something from `6.0.0.0/8` or similar.
